relevance_note: Case series of named individuals with HA20: the paper states that '17 patients from 6 families with heterozygous likely loss-of-function variants in TNFAIP3 (ACMG class 4–5) were finally included' and describes individual patients by label (for example 'Pt16 and pt17 developed depression during adolescence').
method_note: Read only the paper, the schema, the instructions and the rules; no script was used, every row was transcribed by hand from the paper text. In scope: the 17 patients of this study (pt1-pt17, six families) and three previously published people named in the Discussion with at least one individual-level fact (ref 31, ref 32, ref 36). Out of scope (no rows): the counts of previously reported cohorts mentioned without individual detail (177 patients by Elhani et al, 61 by Yu et al, 16 by Aeschlimann et al, 16 by Karri et al and the 'four additional patients with NPSLE' of ref 9, who are described only as a count). Stacked cells (v6, D-31): the supplementary tables are the only source of per-patient features, and in 'Supplementary File 1' every column except 'Pt' is stacked with ' / ' (Age at analysis, Age at onset, Recurrent fever, Oral aphthosis, Genital ulcers, Gastrointestinal disease, Arthritis/tenosynovitis, Skin disease, NPI, Autoimmunity, IS, CXCL9, CXCL10, PGA, CRP); in 'Supplementary File 3' the 'ANA', 'Other autoimmune laboratory findings' and 'Treatments' columns are stacked. I did not assign stacked values to people by position, even when the number of values equals the number of patients. The disease columns hold counts of affected patients per family, not one value per patient: the number of '+' marks per column and family (oral aphthosis 4+2+2+0+3+4=15; recurrent fever 3+1+2+0+1+2=9; genital ulcers 1+2+2+0+2+1=8; gastrointestinal 2+2+1+1+1+2=9; arthritis/tenosynovitis 2+0+0+0+0+1=3; skin 1+1=2; NPI 0+0+1+0+1+5=7; autoimmunity 3+0+0+1+0+4=8) reproduces the counts printed in table 1 exactly (15, 9, 8, 9, 3, 2, 7, 8), so a single '+' in a row with several patients proves nothing about a given patient and stacked values were left 'not reported'. Consequently the checklist is 'observed' only for findings the text names for a person (neuropsychiatric diagnoses for p7, p10, p13, p14, pt15, pt16, pt17; neuropsychiatric involvement for the ref 31 and ref 32 patients; skin lesions for the ref 36 proband) or that a single-patient row states (gastrointestinal disease for pt9). Rows of 'Supplementary File 1' with one patient only are not stacked and were used for pt9 (Age at onset 8, Age at analysis 11, Gastrointestinal disease '+', Autoimmunity '+'); in 'Supplementary File 3' the family 4 row is likewise single-valued (ANA 'Negative', treatment 'Adalimumab'), so pt9 has those too. The ANA column of 'Supplementary File 3' is stacked in every family row (families 1-3 print the same word 'Negative' once per patient, families 5 and 6 print different values), so it was used only for pt9, whose family row holds a single value; there it is recorded in phenotypic_features as the abnormality ruled out ('positive ANA', excluded, D-27) and the composite checklist item 'autoantibodies (ANA/other)' stays 'not reported' because a negative ANA does not exclude 'other' autoantibodies. The group sentence 'none of the patients in our cohort fulfilled the classification criteria for SLE' names the group and is recorded as SLE excluded for pt1-pt17 with evidence_basis 'inferred from group statement'. is_proband is false for pt1-pt17 (the paper calls nobody proband) and for the ref 31 and ref 32 patients; that false value carries no span because no quote supports it. Variant fields were filled only from a statement naming a group that includes the patient: '17 patients from 6 families with heterozygous likely loss-of-function variants in TNFAIP3 (ACMG class 4–5)' gives zygosity, the authors' 'likely loss-of-function' and ACMG class 4–5 for all 17; the per-family ACMG class cell was preferred where available; the authors' own class 'truncating variants resulting in stop codon' is not an enum value and was recorded as variant type 'other', with 'large deletion/CNV' for the family 4 CNV of pt9. Inheritance is 'not reported' for every patient: 'All but one variants were inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern' is a cohort-level statement, the CNV of pt9 is called 'de novo' without any parental testing being reported, and the paper gives no per-person parental carrier statement. Contradictions and oddities: table 1 reports skin involvement in '2 (12)' patients while the two '+' marks sit in family 1 and family 2 rows, i.e. the marks are per-family counts; 'All but one variants were inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern' does not fit the de novo CNV of pt9; the legend of 'Supplementary File 3' does not define '-', so those cells are 'not reported'; the asterisks mark pt4, pt6, pt8, pt11, pt16 as parents and pt12, pt17 as grandparents, which I did not add to the labels. pt1-pt4 were previously described (ref 8, recorded in publications) but source_reference_in_review is 'not reported' for them because this paper presents and reanalyses them first-hand; the citation 20 attached to the CNV of pt9 is not a statement that this patient was published before. The paper gives no sex, age or variant for the ref 31, ref 32 and ref 36 patients, so those fields are 'not reported'.
